title: Visualizing the Strategy
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case for translating an organizational strategy into an actual visual map rather than relying solely on written or verbal explanation. A visual — typically a simple diagram of boxes and arrows connecting premises, actions, and goals — clarifies the causal logic behind the strategy, exposes hidden assumptions, and gives the team something durable to return to and question over time. The piece argues the process of building the visualization is valuable in itself, since inviting the team to challenge the connections tends to sharpen and improve the strategy. It closes with the idea that a well-made visual strategy tends to be self-motivating: seeing the whole picture draws people toward making it happen.
points: A visual map of the strategy clarifies the causal logic connecting actions to outcomes.
